### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleI18nRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f568c1a405854f99dc79f104b5dd89b61819d6d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `afe2101d716a0b9211a0f8c6d1195dcf7c2d424e` — the merge of head `ee54ef8c65b4314ed1e3bcdf896ca146297d8ce0` into base `3f568c1a405854f99dc79f104b5dd89b61819d6d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin afe2101d716a0b9211a0f8c6d1195dcf7c2d424e && git checkout afe2101d716a0b9211a0f8c6d1195dcf7c2d424e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f568c1a405854f99dc79f104b5dd89b61819d6d ee54ef8c65b4314ed1e3bcdf896ca146297d8ce0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f568c1a405854f99dc79f104b5dd89b61819d6d && git merge --no-ff ee54ef8c65b4314ed1e3bcdf896ca146297d8ce0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f568c1a405854f99dc79f104b5dd89b61819d6d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3f568c1a405854f99dc79f104b5dd89b61819d6d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b276ff4e055fb91ec9859c0824ca7b62fe79c497`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts, ui/apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/flowsBundle.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/flowLabels.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/index.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/flow-label-translations.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/stageChangeStarts.tsx, content/docs/ui/translations.mdx

Read: card #36809 with all 7 comments (triage, both claims, the blocked reading 7124251692, the Release, seat route A 7124316383, the done report 7127078995), the PR body, the net diff `origin/main...pr-36916` (18 files, +863/-77), and the 70 check-runs on this head. No earlier contract record exists on the card.

### ① Derived judgments

- `GetLocalesResponseSchema` gains `fallbackChain: z.array(z.string()).optional()`. Accept-set: widened by one optional member; every body that parsed before still parses, and an older client's `z.object` strips the unknown key. Right.
- Public surface, spec: one new authorable-surface key, `api/GetLocalesResponse:fallbackChain`, matching `Metadata-protocol: added`. Right. `Spec property liveness` is success on this head.
- Public surface, wire: `GET /api/v1/i18n/locales` serves the member when `getFallbackLocale()` exists and answers a non-empty string, else omits it. This is the same accessor and the same condition as `metaTranslateOptions` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:3323` and `:3331`). Right. The "one producer" claim holds: `dispatcher-plugin.ts:1752` dispatches into this handler, and `service-i18n` mounts no route (`i18n-route-ledger.ts` header, #23347).
- Carrier: the seat route left the carrier to the dev. `/i18n/locales` over discovery `locale` is sound, since it already carries `sourceLocale` and sits behind the domain's anonymous deny. Right.
- Public surface, `@object-ui/i18n`: new exports `flowsResolveOptions`, `flowsLocaleChain`, `withDeclaredFlowsFallback`, `DECLARED_FLOWS_FALLBACK_KEY`, `DeclaredFlowsFallback`; `flowLabelTranslations` gains an optional fourth parameter. Additive. Right.
- Behaviour, console: `activeFlowsBundle` can now return more than one locale row, and callers that pass `flowsResolveOptions` read a fallback locale before the authored label. This is the card's intent. It is wrong in one case, where the console's language tag is an alias of the authored locale: see M1.
- Gates: all 70 check-runs are success or skipped, including the required contexts (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate) and Check Changeset.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — present on the PR body and in the changeset, and it matches the diff: one optional response member added, nothing removed or narrowed.

The changeset declares `minor` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/console`. `minor` is correct for the spec (new schema member), the runtime (new served member) and `@object-ui/i18n` (new exports). For the other three it is a behaviour change with no removed surface, so `minor` is acceptable. No `!` and no narrowing arm. Check Changeset: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: the done report carries none. The one in the blocked reading (how the console learns the chain) was answered by seat route A, and the diff follows it.
- Dev flag, `flowsLocaleChain` copies the spec's unexported `localeChain`: accepted as flagged. The copy matches `i18n-resolver.ts:747-760` line for line, and a parity pin holds it. Exporting the spec helper is a separate public-surface change.
- Dev flag, the file adapter's collapse means a stack with no `fallbackLocale` serves its `defaultLocale` as the chain: accepted. That is what the server itself walks.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the new reads are two HTTP fetches of existing doors.
- Security: both extra reads go through `i18nFetch` with the session, and the `/i18n` domain denies anonymous callers ahead of every route. Nothing new is exposed to a signed-out caller.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (hits).** The member's shape and its "absent when none is declared" rule hold against `metaTranslateOptions` and `ResolveOptions.fallbackChain` (`i18n-resolver.ts:336-357`). The jsdoc's promise that a client reading it beside `sourceLocale` gets "its answer and the server's walk the same locales" does not hold at its first consumer:

M1 (must-fix) — the console compares its raw language tag to `sourceLocale`, where the server compares the negotiated one, so an alias of the authored locale walks a chain the server skips.
- Server: `metaTranslateOptions` sets `locale: negotiatedTranslationLocale(service, locale)` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:3328-3330`, #36466), which runs `resolveBundleLocale` over `getLocales()`. A `zh-Hans` request in a stack holding `zh-CN` becomes `zh-CN`, `isDefaultLocale` is true, and the chain is not walked: the authored label answers.
- Console: `declaredFlowsFallback` in `loadLanguage.ts` tests `sameTag(lang, declared.sourceLocale)`, a case-fold compare only, and `flowsResolveOptions` passes `locale: language` unnegotiated, so `flowsLocaleChain` and the spec's `localeChain` both see `zh-Hans` against `zh-CN`, treat it as a non-authored request, and consult the fallback.
- Reach: the console's languages are the platform table tags (`BUILT_IN_LANGUAGE_CODES` = `PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS`: `zh-Hans`, `ja`, `es`, `pt-BR`), while stacks and the platform's own bundles spell `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`. So the published page's worked example (`translations.mdx` l.203-207: `defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'`, `fallbackLocale: 'en'`, an `en` bundle) now shows a Chinese console user the `en` flow label where the server answers the authored Chinese. On `main` the console showed the authored label and agreed with the server. This is the #15711 and #36466 defect, reintroduced on the console side for the Simplified Chinese tag the console itself offers.
- It also contradicts this file's own describe line, "Not walked for a request in `sourceLocale`", as a client can implement it from the response alone.
- Evidence level: read from the code on this head, not run. The four new pins use identical tags on both sides (`zh-CN` against `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` against `zh-CN`), so none covers an alias.
- Fix direction: negotiate the console tag as the server does before the authored check and before it is handed to the resolvers. The same `/i18n/locales` answer already carries `locales[].code`, the set `negotiatedTranslationLocale` uses, so `resolveLocaleAmong(lang, codes) ?? lang` gives the server's tag; the `translations` envelope's `locale` is the other source. The describe and jsdoc should say the request tag is negotiated against `locales` first. Add a pin with an alias tag (`zh-Hans` against `sourceLocale: 'zh-CN'`) that asserts no fallback read and the server's answer.

N1 (nit) — "Absent when the server declares none" is looser than the tree. `FileI18nAdapter` defaults `defaultLocale` to `'en'` and the boot collapses `fallbackLocale || defaultLocale || 'en'` (`file-i18n-adapter.ts:165`, `:272-275`), so a file-backed stack that declares neither still serves a chain. The describe could say "when the i18n service reports none". No effect on correctness: the member still equals what the server walks.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts`.** Agrees with the contract sentence by sentence: feature-detected accessor, non-empty string, one-element array, member omitted otherwise, placed after the anonymous deny and the serveable probe. No finding.

**`ui/apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts`.** Carries M1 (the `sameTag` authored check, and the `!sameTag(code, lang)` filter that for the same reason refetches the active locale's own bundle under its other spelling). Otherwise it agrees with its header: the two first reads run in parallel, a failed locale-list read or fallback read degrades to the old answer, a non-spec payload is returned untouched as before, and with no declared chain the resource tree is unchanged.

**`ui/packages/i18n/src/flowsBundle.ts`, `flowLabels.ts`, `index.ts`.** `flowsResolveOptions` carries M1 (`locale: language` unnegotiated). `flowsLocaleChain` equals the spec's `localeChain`. `activeFlowsBundle` skips the reserved entry in its namespace scan, and the other tree scanners (`useObjectLabel.ts:134`, `useSettingsLabel.ts:87`) read `objects` and `settings` members the entry does not hold. The per-key walk in `flowLabelTranslations` (`first`) gives each `nodes` and `screens` key its own fallback, which matches the resolvers' per-string behaviour. The module doc now describes the code. No further finding.

**`FlowRunner.tsx`, `flow-label-translations.tsx`, `stageChangeStarts.tsx`.** Each passes the one `flowsResolveOptions` answer to `translateFlow`, `resolveFlowScreenFieldOptions` and `flowLabelTranslations`. `localizeScreen` overlays the chain in reverse, so the earlier locale wins each copy key. They agree with the contract apart from inheriting M1 through the options.

**`content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`.** "it walks the same chain … as the server's own reads do" is true once M1 is fixed and false until then for an alias tag. No separate finding.

Acceptance against the card: bullet 1 (declared fallback read in the console, matching the server) holds for a non-authored language; bullet 2 (no declared chain: unchanged) holds; bullet 3 (the `activeFlowsBundle` doc) holds. M1 is the case the card's "as the server does" does not yet cover.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36809-flow-labels-fallback-chain`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgv4KRPATgwPAzKKMU`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head b276ff4e · 2026-11-24T09:20Z

L1: REWORK
Head-sha: `b276ff4e055fb91ec9859c0824ca7b62fe79c497`
Reviewer: L1-b (seat 3, area ux-D). Contract review: L2 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` FAIL on this head, comment 7127267955 (claim 7127151797).

### Read
- Net diff `origin/main...b276ff4e` (18 files, +863/−77), PR body, card #36809 with seat route A 7124316383, re-claim 7124864234 and the done report 7127078995.
- Check-runs on `b276ff4e`: every run success or skipped, no failure, none pending; the required contexts and Check Changeset are success. `check-governed-merges --pr 36916`: not governed, 940 changed lines; the card has this one PR, so the card total is 940.

### Checklist
- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36809`. `Fixes` fits once M1 is closed: the three acceptance lines are this PR's whole scope.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added` and `Skills-docs: none` match the claim and the diff: one optional member on `GetLocalesResponseSchema`, one new `api.json` key. The changeset takes `minor` for all six packages, as `Metadata-protocol: added` requires for spec and is right for the runtime and the new `@object-ui/i18n` exports.
- **Producer.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts` reads `getFallbackLocale()` with the same feature detection and non-empty condition as `metaTranslateOptions` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:3323-3331`). The console passes `sourceLocale` as `defaultLocale`, which is what the server passes (declared source, else default). Checked.
- **Console readers.** `flowsLocaleChain` matches the spec's private `localeChain` (`i18n-resolver.ts:747-760`). `resolveBundleLocale` has no catch-all step, so mapping each chain tag cannot pull an unrelated row. The reserved tree entry carries no `objects`, `fields`, `apps` or `settings` member, so the namespace scanners in `useObjectLabel.ts:134` and `useSettingsLabel.ts:87` skip it. The e2e mock that answers `/i18n/locales` with a bare array degrades to the old answer.
- **Tests.** Real commands with output, four new pins named for the card, and two ablations restored byte-equal. None of the pins uses an alias tag; see M1.

### Findings
- **M1 (must-fix), adopted from the L2 record 7127267955.** The console decides "this is the authored language" by a case-fold compare of its raw tag (`loadLanguage.ts` `sameTag(lang, declared.sourceLocale)`), and `flowsResolveOptions` hands the resolvers `locale: language` as is. The server negotiates the tag first (`negotiatedTranslationLocale`, `meta-item-read-gate.ts:3328-3364`, #36466). I re-read both on this head. The console runs in alias tags: its built-in codes are the table tags (`zh-Hans`, `ja`, `es`, see `ui/scripts/check-eager-locale-catalogues.mjs:86`), and `ui/packages/i18n/src/i18n.ts` documents instances in a stored alias (`zh`, `zh-TW`, `pt`). On the page's own example (authored `zh-CN`, fallback `en`), a `zh-Hans` or `zh` console now shows the `en` flow label where the server and `main` show the authored Chinese. Fix: negotiate `lang` against the same answer's `locales[].code` (`resolveLocaleAmong(lang, codes) ?? lang`, as the server does) before the authored check and before it reaches the resolvers. Add a pin with an alias tag against `sourceLocale: 'zh-CN'` that asserts no fallback read and the server's answer.
- **S1 (should-fix), paper only.** Two files sit outside the claim's file surface (7124864234): `ui/apps/console/src/loadLanguage.test.tsx`, where an existing session pin is edited, and `ui/packages/i18n/src/index.ts`, where the barrel gains five exports. Both edits are needed and the PR body names the first. The area posts a claim amendment naming them; no push needed for this one. (`protocol.zod.ts` is covered by "the dev names the carrier", and `api.json` and `protocol.mdx` by regenerated artefacts and API reference docs.)
- **N1 (nit).** `ui/apps/console/src/loadLocales.ts:90` already reads `GET /api/v1/i18n/locales`, and the loader now reads it again on every language load. It costs one request and has no correctness effect. Leave it, or share the answer later.
- **N2 (nit), from the L2 record.** The `fallbackChain` describe says it is absent "when the server declares none", but the file adapter always reports a chain (`fallbackLocale || defaultLocale || 'en'`). "When the i18n service reports none" would be exact. If M1's fix touches this describe anyway, fix it in the same push.

### Delta
The M1 fix moves the head, so it owes a delta L1 and a delta L2 on the new head. S1 is closed by the amendment alone.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ee54ef8c65b4314ed1e3bcdf896ca146297d8ce0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + ui/apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/flowsBundle.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/flowLabels.ts, content/docs/ui/translations.mdx

Delta review of record 7127267955 (head `b276ff4e`, FAIL on M1). Read: the delta `b276ff4e..ee54ef8c` (two commits, 93804689 and ee54ef8c, no merge from main; 7 files, +130/-36), the card's two new comments (claim amendment 7127305468, fix-round report 7128947793), the seat's L1 7127286361, and the check-runs on this head. Everything outside the delta stands as judged in 7127267955.

### ① Derived judgments

- `GetLocalesResponseSchema`: the delta changes the `fallbackChain` describe string and the jsdoc only. Accept-set unchanged, no key added or removed, and `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` is untouched by the delta. Right.
- `@object-ui/i18n`: `DeclaredFlowsFallback` gains an optional `locale`, and the fourth parameter of `flowLabelTranslations` now also accepts `locale`. Both additive. Right.
- Behaviour, console: the active language is negotiated against `locales[].code` before the authored check, the fallback filter and the resolvers. An alias of the authored locale now walks no chain and fetches no fallback bundle, which is the server's answer and the answer on `main`. Right.
- Gates: 61 success and 9 skipped on this head, no failure, including the required contexts. One later re-run of `Check Changeset` (started 10:36Z) was still in progress when read; the earlier run on this head is success and the delta does not touch the changeset.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — unchanged on the PR body and the changeset. The delta publishes nothing new on the wire: a describe string and jsdoc on the spec, one optional type member and one widened optional parameter on `@object-ui/i18n`. The existing `minor` on all six packages covers it; the changeset file is unchanged and needs no edit. `Metadata-protocol: added` still names the one key the PR adds as a whole; the delta itself adds none.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: the fix-round report carries none.
- Dev flag, the duplicate `GET /i18n/locales` read beside `loadLocales.ts` is left as is: accepted. It costs one request per language load, has no effect on correctness, and that file is outside the amended surface.
- Dev deviation, the PR body was not edited for the fix round: accepted. Its declarations are unchanged by the delta; the seat folds the delta in.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The delta adds no query and no fetch.

### ④ Design judgment

M1: closed
S1: closed
N1: closed

N1 is the describe wording of record 7127267955, which the seat's L1 lists as N2. S1 is the seat's L1 finding, closed by claim amendment 7127305468, which names `loadLanguage.test.tsx` and `ui/packages/i18n/src/index.ts`. The seat's own N1 (the duplicate locale-list read) is the accepted deviation under ③.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**How M1 closes, against the server.** `negotiatedTranslationLocale` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:3350-3365`) answers `resolveBundleLocale(offered, requested) ?? requested` over the non-empty string codes of `getLocales()`. `resolveBundleLocale` is an exact own-key match and then `resolveLocaleAmong` over the keys (`i18n-resolver.ts:641-652`), whose first step is the same exact match. The console now runs `resolveLocaleAmong(lang, codes) ?? lang` over `locales[].code`, and `toLocaleDescriptors` maps `getLocales()` one to one (`i18n-resolver.ts:4425-4431`), so the set and the ladder are the server's.
- Exact tag: unchanged.
- Alias (`zh-Hans`, `zh` against `zh-CN`): negotiates to `zh-CN`, the authored check hits, and no entry and no fallback bundle are written. The resolvers then get `{ locale: language }` over a bundle keyed by `language`, which reads the active row and then the authored label, as the server reads `zh-CN` and then the authored label.
- Region or base fallback (`ja` against `ja-JP`): negotiates to `ja-JP`, the entry records it, `flowsResolveOptions` hands it out as `locale`, and `activeFlowsBundle` keys the active row by it.
- Empty `locales` or no match: `resolveLocaleAmong` answers nothing and the raw tag stands, as on the server.
- Failed locale-list read, or no declared chain: `fetchDeclaredChain` answers `null` and the loader gives the pre-PR answer. The server's chain is then the negotiated tag alone, which reads the same row.

**The negotiated tag reaches every reader.** The four call sites on this head (`FlowRunner.tsx:657-658`, `flow-label-translations.tsx:47-49`, `flowLabels.ts:144-148`, `stageChangeStarts.tsx:106-108`) all take `flowsResolveOptions`, so `translateFlow`, `resolveFlowApprovalStepLabel`, `resolveFlowScreenFieldOptions` and `flowsLocaleChain` are asked for the negotiated tag. `flowLabelTranslations` reads `declared?.locale ?? language`. A three-argument caller would ask for the raw tag over a row keyed by the negotiated one, and `resolveBundleLocale` maps the one to the other by the same ladder.

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (hits).** The describe and jsdoc now say the member is absent when the i18n service reports none and that the request tag is negotiated against `locales[].code` before the `sourceLocale` test. Both sentences hold against `metaTranslateOptions` and the file adapter. `protocol.mdx` carries the same string. No finding.

**Pins.** The new cases use alias tags on a `zh-CN`-authored stack with fallback `en` (`zh-Hans`, `zh`), assert no `en` read and equality with the resolver asked as the server asks it, and keep one non-authored alias (`ja` to `ja-JP`) reading the fallback. That is the case the first round's pins missed. Read, not run here; `Test UI` is success on this head.

N3 (nit) — `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` still says the member is "absent when the stack declares none", the wording the schema describe just dropped: a file-backed stack always reports a chain. The new sentence on matching the Console's language is accurate. No effect on correctness; a prose-face fix or a follow-up.

Acceptance against the card: all three bullets hold on this head, the alias case included.
